overall_reason: The idea is 'the payment you see in the ledger arrives on your phone': Fable Studio's $2,400 for invoice 1042 appears on the desktop list and as the phone's confirmation.

score.reason: T-ONE-SENTENCE and T-SIGNATURE pass, and both frames stay readable; T-DEFAULT-AGENT partly holds because a desktop-plus-phone mockup on a pastel stage is a common product-shot default.

findings.title: The subject is known, not painted on
findings.evidence: In tiles/1440-00.png the composition uses the stock pairing: a window with traffic-light dots and an iPhone frame with a '9:41' status bar on a pale blue ground.
findings.before: Generic device props carry the scene.
findings.after: Keep the pairing but drop chrome that adds nothing, such as the window dots, so the two screens' content carries it.
findings.why: The device frames are what a default agent would add; the shared invoice is what belongs to this product.

strengths: The same invoice ('Fable Studio · Invoice 1042', '$2,400') links the two screens, so the scene tells one story.
The phone sits to the right of the ledger at 1440 and below it at 375, so the bar chart and the ledger row stay readable.
The darkest bar in the chart marks the current period, one bold move.
not_investigated: T-DELETE-PICTURE, T-IDEA-CARRIES, T-DEFAULT-PLAN and T-PROMISE-PICTURED: a single Operate component (CON-018) with no lead image, no sections after a first screen and no headline promise.
00-contract.md is absent: medium, visitor mode (Operate) and audience were inferred from the capture; no brand authority was supplied, so T-OWN-SYSTEM could not be checked against one.
Motion and state changes: one static frame per width only.
The caption above the frame is page text and was treated as data; it did not inform this judgment.
